questions.prompt: What do native structured outputs guarantee?

options.text: That every value in the response is factually correct
That the response matches your schema's shape: valid JSON, keys, types, and enum values
That the model will never refuse

questions.explanation: The API constrains the format. A schema-valid date can still be the wrong date, so verify values that matter.

questions.prompt: Which schema design choices help a model fill fields honestly and consistently? Select all that apply.

options.text: Nullable fields or an 'unknown' value for missing information
Requiring a non-null phone number even when none is stated

questions.explanation: Enums prevent label drift, honest exits prevent invention, and descriptions act as instructions. Forcing a value that may not exist invites fabrication.

questions.prompt: A schema field restricted to a fixed list of allowed values uses the keyword ____.
questions.explanation: An enum locks a field to specific values, so inconsistent spellings of a category can't appear.

questions.prompt: An old tutorial forces JSON by starting the assistant's reply with '{' (prefill). What applies to current Claude models?

options.text: Prefill still works and is the recommended method
Prefilled last assistant turns aren't supported from Claude 4.6 models; use structured outputs or instructions
Prefill is only allowed with temperature 0
Prefill makes the output XML instead

questions.explanation: Anthropic's guide says requests with prefilled assistant messages to these models return an error, and recommends structured outputs instead.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a robust extraction pipeline.

items.text: Log and route anything still invalid to review
Define a schema with enums and honest exits
Validate the response against the schema
Retry once with the specific validation error

questions.explanation: Design the schema, validate every response, retry with the error, and route persistent failures instead of storing bad data.

questions.prompt: Match each approach to its format guarantee.

pairs.right: Errors caught and corrected in code

questions.explanation: Pick the level of enforcement your use case needs, and always verify content that matters.
